subject: Post-call: Dedicated sizing workup & deployment mode decision (Ingest.ai)
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
To: Alex Soto <alex@ingest.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — Dedicated sizing inputs we discussed

Hi Alex / team — thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and the asks we teased on the call so we can finalize a baseline Dedicated sizing suggestion. TL;DR: we need a short sizing workshop to pin peak TPS, token mix, and latency SLOs before we send a formal Dedicated proposal.

Summary of what we covered:
- Deployment modes discussed: Hosted API (fastest to ship), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool), Private VPC / on-prem (for encryption & network isolation). You leaned toward Dedicated for predictable throughput and simpler infra ops.
- Core sizing inputs we need from you:
  1) Target sustained TPS and expected peak bursts (e.g., sustained 40 TPS, peak 120 TPS for 5–10m windows)
  2) Token distribution: average request prompt tokens, average generated tokens, % of long-tail (>=1000 tokens) requests
  3) Latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) and whether p99 can be degraded during bursts
  4) Acceptable GPU families (H100 preferred for low latency, A100 or A40 OK for cost tradeoffs)

Action items from us:
- I attached the token profile CSV you dropped into the call (ingest_token_profile.csv). Please confirm or update.
- Karthik will draft a preliminary Dedicated sizing sketch (GPU count, concurrency targets, expected p95 latency) based on your confirmation.
- If procurement needs SOC 2 / security artifacts we can loop security; Laura can handle the compliance packet.

Quick clarifying Qs for you (reply inline where possible):
1) Do you expect most requests to be short (<100 tokens) with rare long-tail? If so, what percentage are long-tail?
2) Any firm limits on p95 latency? 200ms? 300ms?
3) Do you need private VPC now or want to keep that as an option later?

Next step: once you confirm the numbers above we’ll set a 30-min sizing workshop (Karthik + infra + me) and ship a Dedicated estimate + SKU mapping.

— Avery
Avery Johnson
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Alex Soto <alex@ingest.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Rios <m.rios@ingest.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Dedicated sizing inputs we discussed

Thanks Avery — great summary. Answers inline below.

1) TPS: baseline (sustained) 35–45 TPS, predictable daily pattern. Peak bursts hit ~110–130 TPS but only for short windows (5–12 minutes) during heavy batch jobs.
2) Token distribution:
   - ~90% of calls are small: prompt ~40 tokens, gen ~60 tokens (total ~100 tokens).
   - ~9% medium: total ~400–600 tokens.
   - ~1% long-tail: up to 2,500 tokens (these are batch export / summarization jobs run ad-hoc).
3) Latency SLO: target p95 <= 200ms; p99 <= 400ms if possible. We’re sensitive at p95 for user-facing flows.
4) GPU preference: H100 is preferred for latency-critical endpoints; for cheaper batch pipelines we can accept A100 or A40.
5) Private VPC: would like it eventually for data residency, but not required for the initial pilot — Dedicated with strict network controls should be fine.

Procurement note (Maya): please escalate SOC 2 cert and a simple commercial term sheet — we’ll need to run procurement in parallel.

— Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Dedicated sizing sketch (preliminary) — read before workshop

Alex — thanks for the fast responses, they help a lot. Based on your profile (35–45 sustained TPS, peaks ~120 TPS, 90% short ~100 tokens, 1% long 2.5k tokens) here’s a preliminary Dedicated sizing sketch. This is a starting point for the workshop; we’ll refine when we see real qps traces.

High-level recommendation:
- Pilot (cost-conscious): 2x H100 nodes (NVIDIA H100) as primary capacity with burst pool (1x A100) for large batch jobs. This gives headroom for sustained plus short peaks while keeping p95 ~<200ms on short requests.
- Ops config: set concurrency cap per GPU to favor low-latency (small batch sizes for user flows) and route long-tail jobs to a background pool with relaxed p99.

Sizing rationale & numbers:
- Short calls (~100 tokens, 90%): with H100 we can sustain ~30–40 concurrent short requests per GPU depending on model family and quantization. For 45 sustained TPS we recommend 2 H100s with concurrency tuned to 40–50 to maintain p95 < 200ms.
- Peak bursts (120 TPS): rely on burst pool (A100) + ephemeral routing to keep p95 during spikes; autoscale policy to add 1 GPU for 10–15m windows.
- Long-tail (1%): route to a background pool (1x A40 or A100) with higher throughput but looser latency SLO; can also throttle or queue batch exports during business hours.

Operational suggestions:
- Enable prefix/KV caching for frequent prompts to reduce tokens and improve p95.
- Use mixed quantization for batch pools to cut cost (8-bit for batch, full precision for latency-critical).
- Set client-side throttles if you want to hard cap p99 during peak windows.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_estimate_v1.pdf (contains a line-item SKU map, rough monthly OPEX, and an estimated commit level to get preferential pricing).

Next step: propose a 30-min sizing workshop tomorrow or Thursday — I’ll bring a short deck and a few benchmark slides showing token profiles vs expected concurrency. If Maya wants pricing + SOC 2 artifacts we’ll have Laura assemble that packet in parallel.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
